clue.text: Easy to identify this literary character

definitions.text: Easy to identify this literary character

parts.words: Easy to identify this literary character
parts.note: Easy is not an adjective but a surname: the clue asks for the rank that goes before it in the title of Captain Marryat's 1836 sea novel about a young naval officer

explanation.surface: A reader remarks that some character in a book is simple to recognise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Easy' reads as 'simple', but it is Jack Easy, hero of Frederick Marryat's novel Mr Midshipman Easy; the answer is the word that completes his title.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack Easy holds the junior naval officer's rank named in the novel's title, so that rank identifies him.

clue.text: Lisping girl is not to be believed

indicators.note: a lisp turns an S sound into TH, so the word for the girl is said with that speech defect

parts.note: an unmarried girl or young woman is a miss

explanation.surface: Someone warns that a lisping girl is a liar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lisping' turns each S in MISS into TH, giving MYTH; the definition is the fable or falsehood that is not to be believed.
explanation.definitionFit: A fable or invented tale is a story nobody should take as true.

clue.text: Reduces, as included in orders

indicators.note: the word as is placed within the word for orders, so it ends up included in it

parts.note: decrees are official orders
taken as written

explanation.surface: Cutbacks, it seems, are written into official orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orders' could be commands given, but here it means official decrees; 'included in' is the container signal, and the comma is only punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: To diminish something is to make it smaller, a synonym pair.

clue.text: Put out he starts becoming agitated

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of put are knocked out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone put out by events begins to get worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' looks like 'annoyed', but 'out' is the anagram signal for 'Put'; 'starts becoming' simply links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being worked up or flustered is an informal synonym for being agitated.

clue.text: Choose the French condiments

parts.note: to pick is to choose
les is French for 'the' before a plural noun

explanation.surface: A diner is invited to choose the French relishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Preserved vegetables in vinegar are relishes served alongside food, a kind of condiment.

clue.text: Girl able to recall where dates can be found

parts.note: Alma is a girl's name

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the word for able is read backwards

parts.note: if you can do something you are able

explanation.surface: A girl is able to remember where dates are recorded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dates' suggests fruit or romance, but means calendar days; 'to recall' reverses the word for able.
explanation.definitionFit: A yearly calendar of events and data is the book where you look up dates.

clue.text: Cram for a sound public school

indicators.note: sound here means the answer is the spoken form of the school's name

parts.note: Stowe is a well-known English public (fee-paying boarding) school in Buckinghamshire

explanation.surface: A pupil crams to get into a well-regarded public school.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a 'public school' is a private fee-paying school; Stowe is one, and its name is said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To pack items tightly into a space is to cram them in.

clue.text: Trips on the river Loire

explanation.surface: Excursions are offered along the Loire.
explanation.definitionFit: Journeys taken for pleasure are trips; separately, a French city of that name stands on the Loire.

clue.text: Literally, the longest days

parts.note: literally means by letters: the day of the week whose name has the most letters, nine of them, is meant, not the days with most daylight

explanation.surface: Someone complains about the longest days of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests midsummer, but 'Literally' asks for the weekday with the longest name.
explanation.definitionFit: Of the seven weekday names, the midweek one has the most letters, so its plural fits.

clue.text: Airman and royal marine oddly linked together

indicators.note: oddly means arranged in a strange way, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: RM is the abbreviation for Royal Marine

explanation.surface: An airman and a marine walk off side by side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' rearranges AIRMAN plus RM; 'and' only joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking with elbows hooked together is to be joined to a companion, linked together.

clue.text: Act it so as to be understood

indicators.note: the words act it are worked so as to become a new word, a rearrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: An actor is told to play the part in a way that is clear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so as to be' asks you to rework ACT IT into another word; the letters move to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something implied without being stated is understood silently, a synonym pair.

clue.text: Pay a visit after some persuasion?

explanation.surface: Someone drops in once they have been talked into it.
explanation.definitionFit: To call at a home is to visit; to change your mind after coaxing is also this phrasal verb.

clue.text: Count as one of the earliest air-ships

explanation.surface: A nobleman is described as a pioneer of airships.
explanation.definitionFit: Count Ferdinand von Zeppelin was a German noble, and the rigid airships he designed were named after him.

clue.text: Outgoing children

explanation.surface: The offspring are sociable types.
explanation.definitionFit: An outflow or emergence is an outgoing; offspring are one's progeny.

clue.text: The pervading mood all round the world

explanation.surface: A general feeling spreads across the globe.
explanation.definitionFit: The prevailing tone of a place is its feel; the layer of air enveloping the earth also has this name.

clue.text: For wrapping or handkerchiefs — its uses are varied

indicators.note: varied means changed in arrangement, so the letters of its uses are rearranged

explanation.surface: A product for wrapping or for nose-blowing has many different applications.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are varied' rearranges ITS USES; the definition covers both thin wrapping paper and paper hankies.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin soft paper is used for packing gifts, and paper hankies go by the same name.

clue.text: Mounting disorder

explanation.surface: Trouble is on the increase.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting up or ascending is a rising up; a rebellion or revolt is unrest.

clue.text: Put in a demand for medical treatment

indicators.note: treatment means the letters of medical are handled and reworked into another order

explanation.surface: A patient made a request for hospital care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treatment' reads as medical care, but it rearranges MEDICAL; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert a right to something is to ask for it formally, putting in a demand.

clue.text: Raise stake on horse, it may be hotly tipped

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the stake comes below the horse

parts.note: a mount is a horse for riding

indicators.note: raise in a down clue means the word for stake is read upwards

parts.note: an ante is a stake put in before a poker hand

explanation.surface: A punter raises the stake on a horse that is a hot tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise' turns ANTE upwards to ETNA, sitting on MOUNT in this down clue; 'hotly tipped' is racing talk but means a volcano with a hot summit.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sicilian volcano has a peak that glows with lava, a summit that is literally hot.

clue.text: Keep watch

explanation.surface: A guard is told to stay on lookout.
explanation.definitionFit: To honour a rule or festival is to keep it; to notice or look at is to watch.

clue.text: Put into bonds, on account of great interest?

explanation.surface: Someone is enslaved because their curiosity is gripping.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb once meant to enslave; now it means to captivate by holding someone's fascination.

clue.text: Force holds our weapons

indicators.note: the word for force holds the word our inside it

parts.note: an army is a military force
taken as written

explanation.surface: A military force keeps hold of our arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weapons' stands for the place they are kept, a common crossword stretch; 'holds' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A store of arms is a collection of weapons; here the place stands for its contents.

clue.text: Almost a month before a bed bears fruit

indicators.note: before places the shortened month ahead of the bed
almost means the month's name is not quite complete, its last letter lost

parts.note: April is a month
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: Nearly a month before a planted bed yields fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops the last letter of the month; 'bears' is a link meaning 'produces', not part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An orange stone fruit related to the plum is one example of fruit.

clue.text: Covenants to do something in addition to writing

indicators.note: in places the word for doing something inside the abbreviation for an addition to writing

parts.note: PS, postscript, is an addition at the end of a letter
to act is to do something

explanation.surface: Agreements require action as well as written terms.
explanation.walkthrough: PS, the postscript, is the classic 'addition to writing' in crosswords; 'in' is the container signal and 'to' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal agreements binding two parties are covenants, a synonym pair.

clue.text: Key edict of parliament, one raising awkward points

definitions.note: a verb phrase defining a plural noun: plants that put up prickly spines

parts.note: C is a musical key
an act is a law passed by parliament
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A key parliamentary decree is pushed by someone who raises tricky issues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkward points' suggests difficult questions, but means spines, as on desert plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Desert succulents are covered with sharp spines, so they put up prickly points.

clue.text: Hills split internally by floods

indicators.note: internally means the word for split goes inside the word for hills

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor
a rent is a tear or split

explanation.surface: Hills are carved up from within by flooding.
explanation.walkthrough: TORS are rocky hills typical of Dartmoor in south-west England; 'internally' is the container signal, 'by' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Violent rushing streams of water are floods, synonyms.

clue.text: Weird how corpse ends in the lake

indicators.note: how the word corpse ends means its final letter

parts.note: Erie is one of the Great Lakes of North America

explanation.surface: Something strange about a corpse that ends up in a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'how corpse ends' gives its last letter, E, which comes before ERIE; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Strange and unsettling, uncanny, is a synonym for weird.

clue.text: Border left off the shelf

indicators.note: off means the letter for left is taken off the word for shelf

parts.note: a ledge is a narrow shelf

explanation.surface: A border has been left off the shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' removes L from LEDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rim or margin around something is a border, a synonym pair.

clue.text: Nut or nuts

explanation.surface: A madman is mad.
explanation.definitionFit: An oddball is slang a nut; as an adjective, weird or crazy is nuts.

clue.text: Estimated trade turnover

indicators.note: turnover means the letters of trade are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A business's annual turnover has been estimated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turnover' reads as a business's sales figure, but it rearranges TRADE.
explanation.definitionFit: To value or assess something is to estimate its worth, a synonym pair.

clue.text: I've turned left, it's certainly not right

indicators.note: turned means the letters of I've are turned round and read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone who has turned left insists it is definitely wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses IVE to EVI, followed by L; 'right' here is moral rightness, not direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Wicked or morally bad is the opposite of right in the ethical sense.

clue.text: Identical, nevertheless

explanation.surface: Things are alike all the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Exactly alike is identical; as an adverb the phrase also means even so, however.
